prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a downward-angled outdoor masonry scene with a low brick border running diagonally across the lower foreground (~0.8–1.2 m away), a raised red-brick structure to the upper right (~1.5–2.5 m away), scattered hollow concrete blocks on the ground (~1.0–1.8 m away, spaced ~0.2–0.6 m apart), mortar pans on the lower right (~1.0–1.5 m), and a co-worker standing to the right at ~1.2–1.8 m. Across frames 1 to 5, the camera wearer tilts further down and reaches forward so their forearms and a held concrete block appear bright white in the bottom foreground at ~0.3–0.6 m (within arm's reach) in frames 3–5, while the co-worker steps out of view in frame 2, shows only a lower leg in frame 3, and bends down toward the camera wearer in frames 4–5 until their upper torso and extended left hand reach ~0.5–0.8 m to grasp the same block from above and to the right. Both people's heads are out of frame, with the co-worker's torso angled leftward/downward toward the block rather than facing the camera, and the co-worker's bent body partially occludes the ground and stacked blocks behind them on the right in frames 4–5. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the elevated foreground arms, held block, and leaning co-worker from the cluttered dirt, foliage, and similarly coloured blocks below, and makes the vertical relief of the low curb and hollow block cavities immediately apparent. However, the depth map looks unreliable in frame 2 where a large bright flare washes out the lower-left ground plane, and across frames 1–5 where per-frame normalisation shifts the background ground brightness from mid-grey to nearly black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is extremely sparse across the outdoor construction scene, failing to segment the ground, curb, mortar pans, or most concrete blocks, and detecting only a few isolated regions in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5 while leaving frame 2 completely blank. In frame 1, it detects the co-worker's lower body on the right (~1.2–1.8 m away, cropped at the right edge and facing left), the raised brick structure at upper centre-left (~1.8–2.5 m away, ~0.5 m left of the person), and a small plastic bottle (~1.6 m away) between them; in frames 3–4 it segments only the camera wearer's foreground right arm (~0.3–0.5 m, bottom right) and the concrete block within arm's reach (~0.4–0.6 m, bottom centre); and in frame 5 it segments only the bending co-worker at upper right (~0.5–1.0 m away, reaching down into the camera wearer's reach). When masks are present, they sharply delineate the silhouette of the co-worker's legs and leaning torso—even where brightly lit or cropped by the right frame border—and separate the camera wearer's forearm from the held concrete block in frame 3 better than a quick glance at the busy RGB background. However, the map is highly unreliable overall: it completely misses the co-worker in frames 2–4, misses the camera wearer's hands and the transferred block in frame 5, and severely misclassifies nearly every non-person mask (labelling the brick wall as 'cake', the held concrete block and forearm in frame 3 as 'knife' and 'carrot', and the right forearm in frame 4 as 'carrot').
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across all five frames of the construction workspace, detecting only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's right hand in the lower-centre foreground of frame 3 at ~0.4–0.5 m distance. In that third frame, the 21-keypoint hand skeleton shows the wrist entering from the lower right with the thumb and fingers angled upward and to the left, grasping the top-right edge of the hollow concrete block within immediate arm's reach (~0.4–0.6 m in front of and below the camera wearer). Where detected in frame 3, the pose skeleton makes the exact finger articulation and pinch configuration on the concrete rim clearer than in the RGB image, where skin tone and shadow blend against the dirt and stone. However, the pose map is severely unreliable for broader spatial understanding because it provides zero body or hand skeletons in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5—failing to track the co-worker standing ~1.2–1.8 m away on the right in frame 1 or bending to within ~0.5–0.8 m in frames 4–5 because their head and upper shoulders remain cropped out of frame, and missing both the camera wearer's left hand and the co-worker's reaching hands during the block handoff.
